newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NorScan pulp stocks largely unchanged in Dec-Sodra.
newsitem.headline: NorScan pulp stocks largely unchanged in Dec-Sodra.

text.p: Swedish forestry cooperative Sodra on Wednesday said North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp inventories were largely unchanged in December.
"There are still some plants in the U.S. that have not reported their figures, but it seems now that stocks are practically unchanged," Sodra Cell spokesman Hans Burmeister told Reuters.
In November NorScan pulp stocks stood at just over 1.9 million tonnes.
Burmeister said stocks in Sweden in December rose by 54,000 tonnes in Sweden but fell by 9,000 tonnes in Canada, 7,000 tonnes in Finland and 4,000 tonnes in Norway.

"When there were only some U.S. plants left to calculate into the figure, the stocks were down 30,000 tonnes which would mean a slight increase. But U.S. figures are still a little uncertain," he said.
The reason for the rise in Sweden was the number of holiday days at the end of the month.
"We will more than likely compensate for this rise in Janaury thanks to the high level of deliveries we now have," Burmeister said.
